newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Market gets back in gear.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Market gets back in gear.

text.p: Asian debt markets had a lot to offer on Tuesday after putting in a few dull days.
Bankers said the market is starting to get back in gear after slowing last week as emerging markets slumped.
High-yield paper had performed badly following remarks from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that suggested that that the Fed might tighten earlier than many had expected.
"Asian paper proved pretty resilient and market conditions remained stable," remarked on trader. He said Philippine debt was most affected, but prices have improved.
In the latest news from the Philippines, the International Finance Corp today priced the debut peso Eurobond at par. The 2.6 billion peso five-year paper pays a coupon of 10.25 percent.
Elsewhere, Korea Exchange Bank sneaked into the market with a one-year US$100 million floating rate note issue launched via Chase Manhattan International.
The notes pay a margin of 22.5 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate and were issued at 99.945 percent of par. Fees were not disclosed.
The issue pays a lot more than KEB's most recent deal, a one-year FRN launched last December that paid a coupon of LIBOR plus 10 basis points and an all-in of 15 basis points.
The market has been tough for Korean issuers this year as the Hanbo debacle weighs on the banking sector.
Chase Manhattan Asia launched a US$100 million secured guaranteed FRN for a unit of the Berjaya Group, a Malaysian property company.
The five-year notes were issued at 99.80 and re-offered at par. They pay a margin of 140 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 148 basis points.
Some bankers complained that the margin was tighter than anticipated.

Hong Kong Chinese Bank was in the market with a US$70 million subordinated step-up FRN. The notes pay a margin of 137.5 basis points over LIBOR for the first five years and 300 basis points thereafter.
The issue can be called on every interest payment date subject to approval by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. It can be put if certain ownership covenants are violated.
Arranger ING Barings said the issue is attracting a favourable response, helped by the borrower's strong parentage. Hong Kong Chinese Bank is held by HKCB Bank Holdings and China Resources Co.

In loan news from Hong Kong, Chase Manhattan Asia announced that it along with Fuji Bank and Standard Chartered Bank have been chosen as arrangers and bookrunners for a HK$3.0 billion transferable credit facility for SPC Credit.
SPC Credit is a Hong Kong deposit taking company wholly owned by American International Group.
Thai Finance Ministry Amnuay Viravan said that the roadshow for Thailand's planned US$500 million Yankee bond will be postponed to April from mid-March.
Amnuay said the delay stems from his current focus on monitoring the battered Thai financial sector.
Looking ahead, India's ICICI is expected to launch its step-up subordinated bond as early as today. Citicorp and SBC Warburg are the leads.
Roadshows for the seven-year straight bond for Industrial Bank of India start next week. Merrill Lynch is the bookrunner, while BA Asia, ABN Amro and SBC Warburg are joint leads.
Presentations for a structured issue for APP Global Finance also will begin next week, bankers said. Peregrine Fixed Income reportedly will lead the deal.
